title: Pin the Sage plotting surface
objective: Generate and validate exhaustive pinned Sage 10.9.post1 2D and 3D plotting surface artifacts with source hashes and documented classifications ready for the product coverage ledger

oracles: Installed Sage 10.9.post1 module and documentation introspection

handoff.summary: Generated the deterministic SageMath 10.9.post1 plotting authority surface: 49 documented modules (31 2D and 18 3D), 121 module-local public functions, 88 module-local public classes, 328 directly declared public methods, complete signatures, and per-module SHA-256 evidence. Added regeneration documentation and a Sage-independent focused structural test.
risks: The Sagelite wheel omits Cython .pyx sources, so 7 compiled-module hashes explicitly cover the installed Linux x64 extension binaries and will differ across platform builds.

The callable surface intentionally excludes constants, data attributes, private names, protocol methods beginning with an underscore, and inherited-method duplication; later ledgers should add a separately defined artifact if those categories become product requirements.

The full integration attempt recorded 170 passes, 233 failures, and 1 skip because this worktree has no FLINT/FFLAS addons, headers, generated manifests, or production native artifacts. Root integration must rerun it in the provisioned main worktree; the inventory-focused test, strict gate, and architecture gate pass here.
next_steps: Add test/plotting-sage-surface.cjs to the shared Node test manifest and classify sage-surface.json as generated in the integration lane, whose claims own those registries.
Consume schema_version 1 from the coverage-classifier lane, preserving qualified_name as the stable join key and sha256_scope when reporting source provenance.
Run the full integration suite from the provisioned root worktree with FLINT/FFLAS addons and native artifacts available.
